Consult Summary:
- Acute gastroenteritis suspected in a patient with 3 days of loose, watery stools, left-sided abdominal cramps, vomiting at onset, feverish sensation, loss of appetite, and marked fatigue; patient maintaining fluids but reporting significant daily life impact. Conservative management planned with hydration and rest; antibiotics not indicated at this time. Follow-up in 3–4 days or sooner if symptoms worsen; stool testing considered if symptoms persist.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute gastroenteritis (likely viral) presenting over 3 days with loose watery stools (approximately 6–7 times/day), left lower quadrant cramping, vomiting at the start, reduced appetite, and weakness/feeling shaky. No blood in stools or vomit. Fever around onset reported but no measured fever documented. Symptoms affect daily activities; patient remains able to drink fluids.
- Systems review: no hematochezia or melena; no night sweats; no ongoing vomiting at the time of the visit; able to maintain fluids.
- Social history/Medications/Exam findings: Lives with wife and two children; works as an accountant; non-smoker; no alcohol. History of asthma managed with an inhaler; no other meds reported. Abdominal pain described as cramp in left side; no other exam findings documented.
- Differential/Consulting impression: Gastroenteritis (tummy bug); primarily viral with possible bacterial etiology; stool testing if symptoms persist or worsen.
- Plan implications: Hydration and symptomatic care; no antibiotics at this time.

Issue 2:
- Hydration and symptom management plan due to gastroenteritis with diarrheal illness and poor intake. Patient reports ability to hold fluids; guidance to maintain hydration.
- Systems review: able to drink fluids; no current vomiting noted in the visit.
- Medications recommended: oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) to replenish electrolytes; paracetamol for fever/weakness as needed.
- Plan implications: Use Dioralyte for rehydration; monitor for persistence or worsening of symptoms; rest and avoidance of strenuous activity; consider time off work for 2–3 days.

Issue 3:
- Follow-up and potential investigations. If symptoms do not improve or worsen, reassessment planned.
- Timeline: Re-evaluate in 3–4 days; if not improved, stool sample may be taken for testing; further workup to evaluate ongoing symptoms if needed.
- Plan implications: Return sooner if symptoms worsen; possible stool testing/culture if symptoms persist.

Medications:
- Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Dioralyte (oral rehydration) — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- None documented.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma; uses inhaler; well-controlled.

Social History:
- Lives with wife and two children; works as an accountant; non-smoker; does not drink alcohol.

Preventative History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs documented.
- No physical examination findings recorded.

Plan:
- Conservative management for presumed viral gastroenteritis: ensure adequate hydration with oral rehydration solution; avoid unnecessary antibiotics.
- Symptom control: paracetamol as needed for fever/weakness; rest; light foods as tolerated; maintain fluid intake.
- Activity/work: recommend taking 2–3 days off work while infection clears.
- Monitoring: self-monitor at home; seek medical re-evaluation in 3–4 days if not improved; consider stool sample/testing if symptoms persist or worsen; reassess for alternative diagnoses if symptoms persist.

  - Travel history, recent exposures, or pregnancy status (not applicable here).
  - Formal medication reconciliation (beyond asthma inhaler noted in PMH).
  - Preventive care history (not documented).

- Internal conflicts:
